extracted.intended_audience: general public, psychologists, and researchers interested in humor and coping
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes research about how humorous responses to a specific tragedy (Hurricane Sandy) change over time and the role of psychological distance; identifies when jokes about a tragedy are most likely to be perceived as funny. Useful for understanding when it is appropriate/effective to use humor about real-world adverse events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benign violation theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor arises when a situation is both a violation and perceived as benign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article states the findings are consistent with the benign violation theory of humor; this theory explains why some jokes about a tragedy can be funny when the threat is attenuated enough to be perceived as benign while still involving a violation. Use this principle to assess whether an instance (e.g., a joke) constitutes a benign violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological distance as moderator of humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Psychological distance from a tragedy determines whether the event is perceived as threatening or benign, thereby modulating humorous responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time (psychological distance) can buffer people from threat, creating conditions for a benign violation. If distance is too small, the threat dominates and humor is less likely; if distance is too large, the event becomes purely benign and the violation element weakens. This criterion helps decide whether humor about a recent event is likely to be received as funny or offensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal trajectory (rise–peak–fall) of humorous responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Humorous responses to a tragedy do not increase monotonically over time; they rise, reach a peak, and then fall over the observed period (100 days in the study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The longitudinal study measuring reactions to jokes about Hurricane Sandy found a 'comedic sweet spot' within the 100-day window when humor peaked. This implies timing matters: there is an optimal window post-event for humorous treatment before the perceived violation becomes purely benign and funniness declines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of humor in the context of tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor facilitates coping, social coordination, and well-being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article highlights these functions as reasons why humorous responses to tragedy matter. When deciding whether to use or evaluate humor about adverse events, consider whether the humor serves coping, fosters social coordination, or promotes well-being for the audience.
